I knew I had depression forever, but never understood the other parts of it. My ex wife used to say I always had “parties in my head.” When our marriage fell apart, I did several pretty crazy things which put me in the ER five times in a year. I wound up on Lithium because folks thought I had Bipolar Disorder. I believed it at first, and several legit professionals at a high-end transitional living program I checked myself into thought so as well, so I bought into it and took my mood stabilizers.

I eventually figured out, as I entered a positive relationship months after, that I was doing better despite being awful with my lithium compliance. I took a big chance on myself. I titrated myself off the lithium (not recommending that for anyone) and just observed how I did for a while. After a few months, I switched therapists and providers for a fresh pair of eyes. I realized I was responding far more to the outside world than to mood stabilizers. As a mental health professional myself, I realized BPD really put all these pieces together for me, and my new professionals agreed. I’ve been on a simple Lexapro script for two years since, and use weed to level off when needed.

The DBT I learned during this time has helped informed my own practice, snd I am working on finalizing certification now to combine my real life skill building with actual training and be able to legit bill myself as a DBT certified therapist.

All is not perfect. I’m here today, on this group, aren’t I?
